privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.intro: At Cobreo (cobreo.ca), we protect the personal information you share with us. This policy explains what we collect, why, and your rights under applicable Quebec and Canadian law, as well as GDPR principles where relevant.

sections.title: 1. Data controller
sections.body:
Cobreo is responsible for personal information processed through cobreo.ca.

Email: contact@cobreo.ca

Website: https://cobreo.ca

sections.title: 2. Information we collect
sections.body: We may collect: identity and contact details (name, email, phone, company) when you submit a form; the content of your messages or diagnostic answers; technical browsing data (IP address, device type, pages viewed) via cookies or analytics tools if you consent; and information needed to securely operate our internal tools.

sections.title: 3. Purposes
sections.body: We use your data to respond to inquiries, deliver our services, improve the site and our processes, maintain security, meet legal obligations, and — only with consent when required — measure audience or send relevant communications.

sections.title: 4. Legal bases and retention
sections.body:
Depending on context, processing relies on your consent, steps toward or performance of a contract, or our legitimate interests (security, service improvement), in line with applicable law.

We keep data only as long as needed for the purposes described, then delete or anonymize it unless a legal obligation requires otherwise.

sections.title: 5. Sharing and processors
sections.body:
We do not sell your personal information. We may share it with providers that help us host the site, send email, or run our infrastructure (e.g. hosting, database, messaging), only as needed and under appropriate confidentiality commitments.

Some providers may be located outside Quebec or Canada; when that happens, we take reasonable steps to protect your data.

sections.title: 6. Your rights
sections.body:
Depending on applicable law, you may request access, correction, deletion, restriction, portability, or withdrawal of consent. To exercise your rights: contact@cobreo.ca.

You may also file a complaint with the Commission d’accès à l’information du Québec or another competent authority.

sections.title: 7. Cookies
sections.body: See our Cookie policy for categories and how to manage your choices.

sections.title: 8. Changes
sections.body: We may update this policy. The date at the top shows the current version. For material changes, we will adjust the on-site notice as needed.

terms.title: Terms of use
terms.intro: By using cobreo.ca, you agree to these terms. If you do not agree, please do not use the site.

sections.title: 1. Purpose of the site
sections.body: The site presents Cobreo’s services and lets you contact us or start a diagnostic. Content is informational and is not personalized legal, financial, or technical advice until a separate agreement is in place.

sections.title: 2. Acceptable use
sections.body: You agree to use the site lawfully, not to attempt to compromise its security, not to submit illegal or misleading content, and not to use abusive automated means (excessive scraping, spam).

sections.title: 3. Intellectual property
sections.body: Texts, trademarks, logos, designs, and other site elements belong to Cobreo or its licensors. Unauthorized reproduction is prohibited, except for reasonable personal non-commercial use.

sections.title: 4. Forms and communications
sections.body: Information you send must be accurate. We may refuse or ignore abusive requests. An exchange through the site does not automatically create a service contract.

sections.title: 5. Availability and liability
sections.body: We aim to keep the site available and accurate, without guaranteeing uninterrupted access or error-free content. To the extent permitted by law, Cobreo is not liable for indirect damages arising from use of the site.

sections.title: 6. Third-party links
sections.body: The site may link to third-party websites. We do not control their content and are not responsible for them.

sections.title: 7. Governing law
sections.body: These terms are governed by the applicable laws of Quebec and Canada. Disputes will be submitted to the competent courts of Quebec, subject to any mandatory rights you may have.

sections.title: 8. Contact
sections.body: Questions: contact@cobreo.ca

cookies.title: Cookie policy
cookies.intro: This page explains how cobreo.ca uses cookies and similar technologies, and how you can manage your preferences.

sections.title: 1. What is a cookie?
sections.body: A cookie is a small file stored on your device. It may be required for the site to work, or used for analytics and experience improvements depending on your choices.

sections.title: 2. Categories we use
sections.body:
Essential: security, site delivery, remembering your consent and basic preferences. Always on.

Analytics: aggregate usage statistics and session replay (PostHog), only with your consent. Form fields and sensitive diagnostic content are masked in recordings.

Marketing: campaign or promotional measurement when applicable (only with your consent).

sections.title: 3. Legal basis and consent
sections.body: Non-essential cookies are set only after you consent via the banner. You can withdraw consent by clearing browser cookies or contacting us to reset preferences (clearing the local consent key).

sections.title: 4. Duration
sections.body: Duration varies by cookie (session or persistent). Your consent choice is stored locally on your device so we do not ask on every visit.

sections.title: 5. Managing your choices
sections.body: Use the cookie banner on first visit, or clear this site’s data in your browser. You can also restrict cookies in browser settings; some site features may then be limited.

sections.title: 6. More information
sections.body: See also our Privacy policy. Contact: contact@cobreo.ca

diagnostic.title: Analysis tool
diagnostic.subtitle: A few simple questions about how you work — to spot where improvement opportunities may exist.
diagnostic.dimensionMapBody: For each area, say whether it’s part of your activity, whether you want to explore it, or whether it’s not relevant right now.
diagnostic.dimensionMapNeedAll: Set a status for each area to continue.

diagnostic.dimensionSelectNeedOne: Choose at least one area to continue.
diagnostic.radarNeedAnswer: Choose at least one option to continue.
diagnostic.localeFrOnlyNote: The analysis tool is available in English and French.

diagnostic.stagesBody: Select the steps to go deeper on. We’ll only ask about those areas — observable situations, no jargon.
diagnostic.stagesPickHint: Choose at least one section to continue.
diagnostic.introTitle: Spot where you can simplify your operations.
diagnostic.introBody: This is not an audit. In 6–8 minutes, a few simple questions to surface friction in day-to-day work — and make a later conversation more useful.
diagnostic.sectorTitle: What context do you work in?
diagnostic.sectorBody: This only adapts the wording — the questions stay the same.
diagnostic.needChannel: Select at least one channel to continue.

bandHints.high: A lot of friction in your answers — look here first.
bandHints.moderate: Repeated friction: worth a concrete discussion.
bandHints.some: A few signs, less urgent than the priority areas.
bandHints.low: Little friction detected here for now.

questions.acquisition_entry_01: Through which channels do you receive new requests?
questions.acquisition_followup_01: How often are request follow-ups forgotten or delayed?
questions.acquisition_retype_01: Do you have to re-enter the same request information into another tool?
questions.conversion_docs_01: Do you still create quotes or proposals in a highly repetitive way?
questions.conversion_status_01: How easy is it to know where each opportunity stands?
questions.conversion_duplicate_01: Is the same customer data entered in multiple places before a sale?
questions.delivery_manual_01: Are repetitive tasks still done manually around the core work?
questions.delivery_manual_fu: Does this situation involve several people on the team?
questions.delivery_admin_01: How much administrative work still surrounds delivering the work?
questions.delivery_info_01: How often do you need to hunt for information before you can continue working?
questions.coordination_chat_01: Do messages (email, text, chat) often act as the work management system?
questions.coordination_updates_01: Do you regularly need to ask for updates to know where files stand?
questions.coordination_handoff_01: When someone is away, how easy is it for someone else to pick up their work?
questions.admin_billing_01: Does billing preparation still require many manual steps?
questions.admin_sheets_01: Do you use spreadsheets to consolidate information from multiple places?
questions.admin_duplicate_01: Does some information need to be entered in more than one place for admin or billing?
questions.tools_switch_01: Do people have to switch between software tools to complete a single task?
questions.tools_transfer_01: Does some information need to be transferred manually between tools?
questions.tools_transfer_fu: Do these manual transfers happen regularly during the week?
questions.tools_overlap_01: Do several of your tools serve similar functions?
questions.team_absence_01: When an employee is away, how easy is it for someone else to pick up their work?
questions.team_memory_01: Do some reminders or follow-ups mainly rely on people’s memory?

acquisition.low: Few friction signals around inbound requests. This area looks relatively smooth based on your answers.
acquisition.some: A few signals suggest inbound handling or follow-up may be worth a closer look.
acquisition.moderate: Your answers point to possible friction around receiving and following up on requests.
acquisition.high: Several signals suggest inbound request handling could be simplified or better structured.

conversion.low: Little friction detected between request and conversion.
conversion.some: Some signs suggest conversion (proposals, status) could be lightened.
conversion.moderate: Your answers suggest opportunities around proposals, approvals, or duplicate entry.
conversion.high: Several answers indicate strong potential to simplify converting requests into engagements.

delivery.low: Delivery work seems lightly constrained by manual tasks based on your answers.
delivery.some: A few frictions around production or information access could be explored.
delivery.moderate: Your answers suggest some delivery-related tasks may deserve a closer look.
delivery.high: Several signals indicate production and repetitive work around delivery could be simplified.

coordination.low: Coordination looks relatively clear from your answers.
coordination.some: Some signs of manual follow-up or limited visibility appear.
coordination.moderate: Your answers suggest coordination and work visibility could be strengthened.
coordination.high: Several signals point to reliance on messages, memory, or manual status updates.

admin.some: Some billing or consolidation steps could be lightened.
admin.moderate: Your answers indicate moderate potential to simplify administration around the work.
admin.high: Several signals suggest notable friction around billing, spreadsheets, or duplicate entry.

tools.low: Your software environment doesn’t stand out as a major friction source.
tools.some: Some overlaps or manual transfers may be worth reviewing.
tools.moderate: Your answers suggest potential to simplify the software environment.
tools.high: Several signals indicate manual transfers, tool-switching, or overlapping software.

team.low: Little friction related to handoffs or memory-based follow-ups.
team.moderate: Your answers suggest it may help to explore continuity of work across the team.
team.high: Several signals indicate strong reliance on people or memory to keep work moving.

about.title: About Cobreo
about.metaDescription: Cobreo builds custom application solutions: analysis, design, and development for measurable operational impact.
about.heroBody: Cobreo builds custom application solutions. We combine analysis, design, and development to deliver measurable impact — without jargon, with concrete deliverables.
about.originBody1: Across our careers, the same pattern kept showing up — solid companies still wrestling with heavy processes, manual work, and tools that don’t quite fit how they operate.
about.originBody2: We built Cobreo to help businesses spot those improvement opportunities, then design simple solutions rooted in their reality and able to create concrete value. The AI tools available today let us explore, iterate, and prototype much faster — without losing control over decisions and the quality of the outcome.
about.foundersBody: Passionate people, united by the same focus on efficiency — and a shared aim to make a real difference for SMEs.
about.founder1Bio: Product, design, and development: clarifying the need, prototyping quickly, and shipping tools teams actually want to use.
about.founder1Experience: Background in development and design — notably in health and education.
about.founder2Bio: Development and delivery: turning clear intent into a reliable, maintainable solution that fits day-to-day work.
about.founder2Experience: Background in finance, hospitality, and automation.
about.approachBody: Our experience in design and development helps us know where to focus. New AI tools let us explore, prototype, and validate solutions much faster. We use them as an accelerator while keeping control over decisions, design, and final product quality.
about.workBody: We identify the best opportunities, validate before building, deliver tools tailored to your operations, then evolve them with you.
about.ctaBody: A short conversation to clarify your priorities and see how we can help.
